requested_order.text: Wegovy (semaglutide) 0.25 mg SC once weekly x4 weeks, then titrate per label to 2.4 mg weekly

weight_management_program.text: Home exercise program for rotator cuff and scapular stabilizers (band external rotation, rows, scapular retraction, sleeper stretch) daily x 6 weeks. Avoid repetitive overhead work where possible. Follow-up 6 weeks; MRI if not improving.

PHYSICAL THERAPY — 02/08/2026
Mechanical low back pain after lifting stock at work, 4 weeks, no radicular signs.
Plan of care: 6 visits; core stabilization home exercise program daily (dead bug, bird dog, bridges); hip hinge and lifting mechanics training.

GASTROENTEROLOGY PROCEDURE NOTE — 05/22/2026
Screening colonoscopy, age 49 (average risk).
Prep: clear liquid diet the day before, split-dose PEG; good prep.
Findings: two sessile polyps (4 mm, 6 mm) in the transverse colon removed by cold snare; small internal hemorrhoids.
Plan: resume regular diet today; pathology pending; repeat interval per pathology.

S: 49 y/o M, visit for weight, BP, and pre-travel planning. Weight: weight history — 113.4 kg in mid-December 2025 when he started a dietitian-led weight management program; today 112.7 kg. Since mid-December he has followed a portion-controlled plate method with a daily food diary (~1800 kcal/day) and walking about 30 minutes 3 days a week, with monthly program check-ins with the dietitian. Minimal weight change despite consistent adherence, confirmed by his food diary and program attendance record. Asks about Wegovy. No MTC/MEN2 history, no pancreatitis, no gallbladder disease. BP: home readings 120s–130s/70s–80s on amlodipine; no side effects. Travel: Tanzania in October (Kilimanjaro + safari); vaccines partially done at pharmacy. Other: low back pain resolved after PT; albuterol rarely needed;

A/P:
1. Obesity, BMI 36.8 — minimal response to a structured program. Plan: start semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly (Wegovy) with standard dose titration; counseled on GI side effects, hydration at altitude, and holding dose escalation around the trek. Continue plate method and walking. Recheck in 3 months.
2. Hypertension: BP 127/81 on amlodipine 5 mg daily; continue.
3. Pre-travel — typhoid and hepatitis A given at pharmacy per patient; malaria prophylaxis (atovaquone-proguanil) and acetazolamide to be prescribed at travel visit next month.
4. Exercise-induced bronchospasm — albuterol PRN before exertion; bring inhaler on trek.

no_concurrent_glp1.text: CC: left shoulder pain. HPI: 47 y/o right-hand-dominant M with 3 months of left shoulder pain with overhead reaching (stocking shelves at his hardware store) and lying on the left side at night. No trauma, no numbness/tingling, no neck pain. Vitals: Wt 115.4 kg, BMI 37.7, BP 131/78. Exam: no atrophy. AROM full with painful arc 70–120°. Positive Neer and Hawkins-Kennedy. Empty can mildly painful, strength 5/5. External rotation strength 5/5. Negative drop-arm, negative lift-off. Cervical spine exam benign. Imaging: shoulder X-rays — type II acromion, no calcific tendinitis, AC joint mild degenerative change. Assessment: left shoulder subacromial impingement / rotator cuff tendinopathy. Plan: subacromial corticosteroid injection (triamcinolone 40 mg + lidocaine) performed under sterile technique — good immediate relief.

IMMUNIZATION VISIT — 01/30/2025
Influenza vaccine requested (missed fall dose; household member recently had influenza A).
Screening: no fever today, no prior vaccine reactions, no GBS history, no severe egg allergy.
Administered: influenza vaccine 0.5 mL IM, left deltoid, lot recorded. VIS provided and reviewed.
Observed 15 minutes — no reaction.
Also reviewed: Tdap last 2018 (up to date); COVID vaccine last 2023 — updated dose recommended; patient will schedule at pharmacy. Shingles vaccine discussed for age 50.

PHARMACIST MEDICATION REVIEW — 05/21/2025
Pt brought in a bag of OTC products for review: magnesium citrate, turmeric/curcumin, a "prostate health" saw palmetto blend, melatonin 10 mg, and a multivitamin.
Current meds: amlodipine 5 mg daily, sertraline 50 mg daily, cetirizine 10 mg PRN, triamcinolone 0.1% cream PRN.
Review: no clinically significant interactions. Recommended melatonin at a lower dose (1–3 mg); saw palmetto evidence limited — discuss urinary symptoms with PCP; magnesium citrate may loosen stools. Curcumin fine at label doses. Updated OTC list in chart. Pt understood.

LAB RESULT NOTE — 10/15/2025
25-OH vitamin D 24 ng/mL — low. Recommend vitamin D3 2000 IU daily OTC; recheck in 6–12 months. Low vitamin D is common in winter months and with limited sun exposure (works indoors).
Other labs from the same draw (CBC, CMP) reviewed separately — normal. Released to portal with explanation; patient replied he will start the supplement.

OUTSIDE RECORDS — SCANNED — 08/25/2025
Source: Downtown Family Dentistry
Medical clearance for two extractions (#30, #31) and bone graft under local anesthesia. HTN controlled on amlodipine; no anticoagulants or antiplatelets; no bisphosphonates. Cleared for procedure without restrictions; take amlodipine the morning of the procedure.

URGENT CARE — 02/13/2026
48 y/o M with chest tightness, wheeze, and cough starting about 5 minutes into jogging on cold mornings over the past 2 weeks; resolves within 20–30 minutes of rest. No exertional chest pain radiating to arm/jaw, no syncope, no symptoms at rest. ECG: NSR, no ischemic changes.
Exam: lungs clear, SpO2 98%, BP 128/80.
Assessment: exercise-induced bronchospasm; cardiac etiology considered less likely given pattern and normal ECG.
Plan: albuterol 2 puffs 15 minutes before exertion; warm up gradually; scarf over mouth in cold air. PCP follow-up — consider stress test given age/HTN if any atypical symptoms.

PATIENT PORTAL MESSAGE — 05/17/2026
Pt: "Taking my wife to Tanzania (Kilimanjaro trek + safari) in October. What vaccines and meds do we need?"
RN reply: Hepatitis A and typhoid recommended; yellow fever vaccine is generally not required for travel directly from the US but may be required if transiting through certain countries — confirm itinerary. Malaria prophylaxis recommended for safari areas. Acetazolamide can be considered for the Kilimanjaro climb. Given your blood pressure and inhaler use, please schedule a pre-travel visit at least 6 weeks before departure.
